faq_heading: Learning and Development Survey Questions FAQ

plan.angle: The top 10 are long lists of training feedback and career development questions (SurveyMonkey, Paycor, AIHR, SmartSurvey), one analytics blog and a Reddit thread, and none says which question belongs at which point of a program. This page sorts learning and development survey questions by the moment they are asked and the decision they feed: a skills check before the training plan, a knowledge check right after a session, a 90-day follow-up that asks the learner and the manager the same question, and a career goals survey that sizes next year's cohorts. Each tab ends in a decision an L&D lead made from the answers, and the how-to maps questions to the four Kirkpatrick levels, sourced to Kirkpatrick Partners.
tab_stories: Thornfield Freight asks its 48 shift supervisors to rate their confidence in 5 skills from 1 to 5 before it sets the year's training plan; 44 answer, coaching averages 2.6 against 4.3 for safety rules, and the first workshop of the year is on coaching.

Tregarth Software sends its 36 account managers 2 ratings and a 5-question knowledge check after a 2-day negotiation training; 34 answer, relevance averages 4.4, and 15 of 34 miss the question on setting a walk-away price, so the trainer adds a role play on it.

Vinterly Home Care asks the 22 graduates of its new-manager program and each graduate's director the same question 90 days later; 20 graduates say they hold a weekly one-on-one with every direct report, directors confirm 13, and the L&D lead gets a Slack message listing the 7 pairs that disagree.

Osterbrook Analytics asks 120 employees which skill they want to grow this year and how they prefer to learn; 96 answer, 38 pick SQL, 52 prefer learning from a colleague, and the first cohort is an 8-week SQL group with peer mentors.

claims_to_source: The Kirkpatrick model's Level 1 Reaction measures whether the audience finds the training favorable, engaging and relevant
The Kirkpatrick model's Level 2 Learning measures whether the audience acquires the intended knowledge, skills, attitude, confidence and commitment
The Kirkpatrick model's Level 3 Behavior measures whether the audience performs the critical behaviors on the job
